# Sirach Chapter 33 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 33 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_033_page_001.jpg

---

**33:1** No evil will befall the man who fears the Lord, but in testing he will be rescued time and again.

**33:2** A wise man will not hate the law, but the one who acts hypocritically toward it is like a ship in a storm.

**33:3** A sensible person will trust in the law, and for him the law is as reliable as a divine oracle.

**33:4** Prepare what you will say and you will be heard; bind together your learning and then answer.

**33:5** The heart of a fool is like a wagon wheel, and his thoughts like a spinning axle.

**33:6** A sarcastic friend is like a stallion horse; he neighs under everyone who mounts him.

**33:7** Why is one day more excellent than another, when all the daylight throughout the year comes from the sun?

**33:8** They were differentiated by the knowledge of the Lord, who made the seasons and festivals varied.

**33:9** Some of them he exalted and hallowed, and some of them he made into ordinary days.

**33:10** All human beings come from the soil, and Adam was formed from the earth.

**33:11** In the fullness of his knowledge the Lord distinguished them, and made their paths different.

**33:12** Some of them he blessed and exalted, some he set apart and drew near to himself; some of them he cursed and humbled and removed from their station.

**33:13** Like clay in the hand of the potter — to be shaped in whatever way he pleases — so human beings are in the hands of their Maker, to be treated as he determines.

**33:14** Good is the counterpart of evil, and life the counterpart of death; so the sinner is the counterpart of the devout person.

**33:15** Consider all the works of the Most High: they come in pairs, each the opposite of the other.

**33:16** I too was the last to wake up, like one who gleans behind the grape-gatherers; by the Lord's blessing I advanced, and like a grape-gatherer I filled my wine press.

**33:17** Consider that I have not worked for myself alone, but for all who seek instruction.

**33:18** Hear me, you leaders of the people, and you rulers of the assembly, give ear.

**33:19** Do not give authority over yourself to son or wife, brother or friend, while you still live, and do not give your property to another lest you regret it and must ask for it back.

**33:20** As long as you are alive and have breath, do not let any person take your place.

**33:21** For it is better that your children should be dependent on you than that you should look expectantly at the hands of your sons.

**33:22** In all your activities maintain mastery; let no one bring a stain upon your honor.

**33:23** When the days of your life come to their end, at the moment of death, distribute your inheritance.

**33:24** Fodder and stick and burdens for a donkey; bread and discipline and work for a slave.

**33:25** Put your slave to work and you will find rest; leave his hands unoccupied and he will seek his freedom.

**33:26** Yoke and strap will bow the neck; for a malicious slave there are instruments of torture.

**33:27** Assign him work so that he does not remain idle; for idleness teaches great harm.

**33:28** Set him to work, as is appropriate for him; and if he does not obey, make his chains heavier.

**33:29** But do not be overbearing toward anyone, and act with discernment.

**33:30** If you have a slave, let him be to you like yourself, because you have acquired him by blood.

**33:31** If you ill-treat him and he goes out and runs away, on what road will you seek him?

**33:32** There is a path of shame, and there is a path of honor; and for those who are upright there is a path to find him.

**33:33** Now my soul delights in wisdom's instruction, and I speak of it without embarrassment.
